name: button-group
description: Joins buttons into one segmented control: adjacent borders collapse, middle corners square off, and only the outer corners stay rounded — a single outline around the group.
designIntent: Related actions (view modes, zoom, toolbar steps) should read as one instrument, not scattered pills. ButtonGroup collapses adjacent borders with negative spacing so the joined outline matches InputGroup's single-border language, while focus rings lift above siblings instead of being clipped.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Stacked segments share vertical edges; default lays them side by side.

examples.title: View mode toggle
examples.description: Three segments share one outline; aria-label names the group.

examples.title: Vertical toolbar steps
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup orientation="vertical" aria-label="Step navigation">
  <Button variant="secondary">Step back</Button>
  <Button variant="secondary">Step forward</Button>
</ButtonGroup>

examples.title: Stepper with primary action
examples.description: Mix variants freely as long as each button keeps a border.

antiPatterns.title: Don't use borderless variants inside
antiPatterns.explanation: Ghost/link buttons carry no border, so the joined outline breaks at that segment. The group's single-outline promise depends on every segment contributing an edge.

antiPatterns.title: Don't group unrelated actions
antiPatterns.explanation: A joined outline asserts the segments are alternatives of one control. unrelated actions should stay separate Buttons so their relationship isn't overstated.

accessibility.implementation: Renders role=group; pass aria-label (or aria-labelledby) so the group name is announced before its buttons
accessibility.userRequirements: Always provide an accessible name for the group

accessibility.implementation: Focused segments get position:relative + z-10 so the ring paints above neighbours instead of clipping
accessibility.userRequirements: Don't override with overflow:hidden on the group

accessibility.implementation: Buttons keep native tab order; groups are not roving-tabindex widgets (use Tabs for that pattern)
accessibility.userRequirements: When segments behave like exclusive views, prefer Tabs/segmented semantics

guidelines: Keep labels short enough for one line
Lead with the noun or verb consistently (don't mix)

compositionRules.relationship: Direct children — each keeps its own variant/size but must keep a border
For exclusive views with panels, use Tabs; ButtonGroup is for actions/tools, not view switching with content
